(a) 
The President shall appoint, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, two additional district judges for the northern district of California, two additional district judges for the southern district of California, three additional district judges for the District of Columbia, one district judge for the northern and southern districts of Florida, one additional district judge for the northern district of Georgia, one additional district judge for the district of Kansas, one additional district judge for the district of New Jersey, four additional district judges for the southern district of New York, one additional district judge for the district of Oregon, two additional district judges for the eastern district of Pennsylvania, one additional district judge for the southern district of Texas, and the existing judgeship for the western district of Oklahoma created by section 2 (a) of the Act entitled “An Act to provide for the appointment of additional district and circuit judges”, approved May 24, 1940 (54 Stat. 219), and the existing judgeship for the northern district of Ohio created by the Act entitled “An Act to provide for the appointment of one additional United States district judge for the northern district of Ohio”, approved May 1, 1941 (55 Stat. 148),shall be permanent judgeships.     (b) 

        (1) 
Title 28, United States Code, section 134, is amended by adding at the end thereof the following new subsections:


“(c) 
One of the district judges for the district of Kansas shall reside at Wichita; and in the event such judges disagree as to which of them shall reside at Wichita, the matter shall be determined by the Judicial Council of the Tenth Circuit.


“(d) 
One of the district judges for the southern district of California shall reside in the city of San Diego.


“(e) 
One of the district judges for the southern district of Texas shall reside within that portion of the district comprising Laredo, Brownsville and Corpus Christi divisions.”



 
        (2) 
The judge first appointed for the district of Kansas under the authority contained in subsection (a) shall reside at Wichita.
  
    (c) 
The President shall appoint, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, one additional district judge for the western district of Pennsylvania: Provided, That the first vacancy occurring in the office of district judge in said district shall not be filled.

 
    (d) 
The President shall appoint, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, one additional district judge for the southern district of Texas: Provided, That the first vacancy occurring in the office of district judge in said district shall not be filled.

 
    (e) 
The Act entitled “An Act to provide for the appointment of one additional United States district judge for the northern district of Ohio”, approved May 1, 1941 (55 Stat. 148), is hereby repealed and  the incumbent of the judgeship created by such Act shall henceforth hold his position under title 28, United States Code, section 133, as amended by this Act.
 
    (f) 
Section 2 (a) of the Act entitled “An Act to provide for the appointment of additional district and circuit judges”, approved May 24, 1940 (54 Stat. 219), is amended by striking out “western district of Oklahoma”, and the incumbent of the judgeship created by said Act for the western district of Oklahoma shall henceforth hold his office under title 28, United States Code, section 133, as amended by this Act.

fable.w: The section creates federal district judgeships and sets residency requirements for the judges. The tempting reading is that "advice and consent of the Senate" or the dispute referral to the Judicial Council of the Tenth Circuit is consultation, but the Senate and the Judicial Council are both inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, given a hearing, or granted a right to sue over a federal decision.
fable.s: The President shall appoint, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, two additional district judges for the northern district of California

qwen_block.w: This section establishes new federal judgeships and outlines the appointment process for federal judges. The involvement of the Senate (advice and consent) is an intra-governmental process, as Congress is considered inside the federal government. There is no requirement for consultation or coordination with parties outside the federal government, such as states, local governments, or the general public.
qwen_block.s: The President shall appoint, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, two additional district judges for the northern district of California...
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "advice and consent of the Senate" constitutes participation because the Senate is involved in the decision. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress, its committees, and its members are INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, intra-governmental processes like Senate confirmation do not count as participation. The section describes the creation of judicial positions and the internal appointment process for federal judges, with no requirement for consultation with states, the public, or other outside entities.

opus.w: This section creates and adjusts federal district judgeships and sets where some judges must live. The only bodies involved in these decisions are the President, the Senate (through advice and consent), federal judges and the Judicial Council of the Tenth Circuit, all of which are inside the federal government. There is no public comment, hearing, outside advisory body, consultation with states or tribes, or right for anyone to sue. So the procedural wording does not count as participation.
opus.s: in the event such judges disagree as to which of them shall reside at Wichita, the matter shall be determined by the Judicial Council of the Tenth Circuit
opus.b: 1. **The tempting reading:** The section says judges are appointed "by and with the advice and consent of the Senate," and it says the Judicial Council of the Tenth Circuit will settle any disagreement between judges. Both sound like consultation before a decision. That reading fails because the Senate and the Judicial Council are both part of the federal government. Nobody outside the government takes part in any decision here.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes the number of federal judgeships and the process for appointing judges. The appointment process involves the President and the Senate. According to the definition, Congress and its members are inside the federal government. Therefore, the advice and consent of the Senate is an intra-governmental process, not participation by an outside party. There is no consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_chat.s: The President shall appoint, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, two additional district judges for the northern district of California...
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "advice and consent of the Senate" constitutes participation because Senators are involved in the decision to appoint judges. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress, its committees, and its members are INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, interaction between the President (Executive) and the Senate (Legislative) is intra-governmental coordination, not participation by an outside party.
